title: Competitive Signal Runbook: Emerging Model Features and Market Scenarios
creator: Asha Rao
description: Create an operational runbook and prioritization rubric for tracking emergent features and competitive signals from the open and commercial model landscape. This ticket formalizes how PM, RD (research), and GTM ingest signals (new capabilities, latency/cost wins, function-calling behavior, privacy/TCFP claims), triage them for product fit, and route them into roadmap candidates or watchlist actions.
background: We have multiple ad-hoc trackers for model releases, vendor blog posts, and benchmark leaks. Signals are often lost or over-weighted by recency. Engineering and Research need a consistent, lightweight triage to decide if a model change requires product work (support, rollout policy changes, SDK adjustments) or just continuous monitoring. This runbook focuses on feature-level signals (e.g., structured output reliability, multimodal capabilities, low-token pricing for embeddings) rather than model brand announcements.
goals: Define signal categories and severity tiers for model feature changes
Create a repeatable ingestion pipeline and ownership model for incoming signals
Provide a prioritization rubric that maps signals to product responses (watchlist, spike, roadmap, immediate mitigation)
Publish clear operational playbooks for PM->Eng->Research handoffs and follow-ups
success_metrics: Time from signal ingestion to decision <= 5 business days for high-severity signals
Percentage of high-severity signals with a documented action (watchlist/spike/roadmap) >= 90%
Reduction in duplicate signals and input noise by 40% after runbook adoption
> 70% satisfaction from Eng/Research/Support on clarity of next steps (survey)
scope: Covers competitive signals about model capabilities and economic claims from public releases, partner briefings, benchmark results, and customer escalations. Excludes vendor contract/legal evaluation, which remains handled by Legal/Procurement. Focus is product response, not procurement decisions.
deliverables: Signal taxonomy document (categories, examples, severity tiers)
Triage rubric with scoring template and decision matrix
Single-page runbook for on-call PM/Research with escalation path
Automated watchlist spreadsheet (seed data + ingestion template) and a Slack alerting pattern
One internal workshop recording and summary notes for cross-team adoption
key_risks: Signal fatigue leading to ignored high-value inputs
Misclassification of economic claims (pricing tiers) causing incorrect roadmap changes
Insufficient engineering capacity to respond to multiple high-severity signals simultaneously
Runbook not adopted because it's too heavy or unclear ownership
mitigation_plans: Limit ingestion fields to 7 structured attributes to reduce noise
Require a single PM owner assignment per signal with 48h acknowledgement
Create a preapproved contingency budget for one engineering spike per quarter for high-severity competitive regressions
Run two short adoption workshops and embed runbook into weekly PM sync for first quarter
